# Egress lanes of the DRIVER corpus that a consumer may GATE on.
# One lane id per line, in the `kind_str()` vocabulary of `ProviderEntry`
# (anthropic-api, openai-compat, openai-responses, bedrock, gemini).
# Blank lines and `#` comments are ignored.
#
# Plain text on purpose: the whole content of this file is a set of
# tokens, so a schema would add a parse surface and nothing else.
#
# Gating applies ONLY to the driver-generated corpus. Live-box captures
# under tests/fixtures/captured/ are report-only and are never gated,
# whatever this file says.
#
# NAMES ZERO LANES, deliberately, and that is the honest state rather
# than an unfinished one: the driver corpus under tests/fixtures/driver/
# is empty, so there is no lane any consumer could gate on. An entry
# here that no committed fixture backs would be a decorative gate.
#
# The reader is FAIL-CLOSED: with no lane listed it returns
# NoLanesListed rather than an empty gated set, so a consumer cannot
# mistake "not yet populated" for "gate passed". Only the conservation
# harness maps that one variant onto "no lane gated", and it announces
# the emptiness on its own output line.
#
# POPULATED BY the first successful driver capture -- add the lane the
# landed fixtures actually ride, read off the capture, never the lane
# hoped for. The harness carries a self-invalidating test pinning this
# file's current comment-only parse outcome; turning it red is the
# review moment that first entry deserves.
